title: Cross-layer capacity probing and fidelity sampling protocol
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview

This document defines a repeatable protocol for cross-layer capacity probing and fidelity-aware sampling used by the runtime performance and benchmarking teams. The goal is to produce deterministic, signal-rich datasets that drive scheduling, kernel selection, and model-variant routing decisions while preserving production safety.

Goals

- Measure usable capacity and safe degradation points across the full stack (dispatcher -> scheduler -> kernel -> kvcache).
- Correlate fidelity changes (quantization, sharding, batching) with cost and error surface.
- Produce automatable data and thresholds for runtime admission controllers and canary policies.

Scope

- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private runtime variants that use the runtime-dispatcher and kernel-allocator services.
- Focused on core token-generation workloads (chat, standard completion) and embedding workloads where applicable.
- Excludes long-running offline training jobs and third-party accelerator tests unless explicitly scheduled.

Terminology

- Probe: A controlled synthetic traffic pattern used to stress a subsystem.
- Cohort: A grouping of similar requests (seq_len, prompt shape, model variant).
- Fidelity step: A discrete change in model execution (e.g., int8 -> int4, kv cache disabled, half-precision -> full-precision).
- Safe degradation point: The earliest observed point where SLOs are broken for >5% of traffic in a cohort and recovery is non-deterministic.

Ownership

- Author: Jordan Kim (Runtime Performance)
- Primary owners: runtime-performance (eng), kernel-schedulers (eng)
- Observability steward: Priya Nair (Eng Platform)

Required signals & SLOs

Collect the following signals for each probe run:

- request_id (string)
- timestamp (ISO-8601)
- cohort_id (string)
- model_variant (string)
- seq_len (int)
- tokens_generated (int)
- kernel_id (string)
- kernel_latency_ms (float)
- dispatcher_queue_ms (float)
- kvcache_hit (boolean)
- gpu_util_pct (float)
- gpu_mem_used_mb (int)
- host_mem_used_mb (int)
- error_class (string | null)

Minimum SLOs to compare against in probing runs:

- p95 tail latency (generation end-to-end) <= 200 ms for seq_len <= 64 on standard variants.
- p99 <= 800 ms for seq_len <= 64.
- p95 CPU/GPU utilization should not exceed target utilization by more than 12 percentage points for normal ops.

Protocol steps (runbook)

1) Prepare experiment harness

- Create or reuse a synthetic corpus that mirrors the cohort profile (use request-surface-replay tool).
- Configure a probe matrix: cohorts x fidelity-steps x target-utilization (40%, 65%, 85%).
- Pin the runtime image and kernel bundle used for the baseline.

2) Baseline run (no degradation)

- Run each cohort at 40% target-utilization for 30m.
- Record all signals and confirm observability pipes (zipkin/traces, metrics, and probe dataset ingest).
- Validate that baseline SLOs are met; if not, abort and create an action ticket.

3) Fidelity steps and progressive pressure

- For each fidelity change (e.g., int8->int4, reduced KV cache capacity, smaller beam size), run the cohort at target utilizations in increasing order: 40%, 65%, 85%.
- Each run duration: 20m steady-state after 5m warmup.
- If any run breaches p99 latency target or shows >5% error_class != null, mark that combination as degraded.

4) Controlled overload probing

- For candidate safe-degradation points, perform a controlled overload: ramp utilization by +5% per minute until p95 or error thresholds violated or max 100% util reached.
- Capture kernel-level traces for 1 minute windows centered on threshold-crossing events.

5) Automated analysis and threshold extraction

- Run the probe-analyze job to extract: usable_capacity_per_cohort, degradation_onset_util, kernel_breakpoint_map (kernel_id -> seq_len -> latency slope).
- Persist outputs to the benchmarking dataset namespace with tags: commit, runtime-image, kernel-bundle, probe-id.

Data collection schema (text table)

| field | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| probe_id | string | unique id for the probe run |
| cohort_id | string | cohort signature (seq_len_distribution + prompt-type) |
| fidelity_tag | string | description of fidelity step |
| util_target_pct | int | requested target utilization |
| observed_gpu_util_pct | float | observed per-GPU utilization |
| p50_latency_ms | float | generation p50 |
| p95_latency_ms | float | generation p95 |
| p99_latency_ms | float | generation p99 |
| error_rate_pct | float | fraction of requests with error_class != null |

Experiment harness sample config (YAML)

```
probe_id: probe-2026-02-08-crosslayer-01
runtime_image: runtime:v2026.02.01
kernel_bundle: kernels/2026-01-28/optimized
cohorts:
  - id: chat-short
    seq_len_dist: [8, 16, 32]
    qps: 400
fidelity_steps:
  - tag: baseline-int8-kvcache-on
  - tag: int4-kvcache-on
  - tag: int4-kvcache-limited
util_targets: [40, 65, 85]
run_duration_min: 20
warmup_min: 5
observability_endpoints:
  metrics: prometheus.cluster.local:9090
  traces: zipkin.cluster.local:9411
```

Analysis and decision criteria

- Usable capacity: the highest util_target where p95 and error_rate_pct are within SLO thresholds for two consecutive runs.
- Safe degradation point: the util at which p99 is exceeded OR error_rate_pct rises >5% compared to baseline, and the kernel_breakpoint_map shows non-linear latency slope for critical kernels.
- Kernel pin recommendation: if kernel latency slope crosses >2x per additional 10 tokens for a cohort, recommend pinning to alternative kernel_id or fallthrough policy in the scheduler.

Rollout / automation gates

1. Generated thresholds and recommendations are pushed to the staging runtime-operator via the probe-ci pipeline.
2. Staging will run a lightweight canary (10% traffic) for 24h with automatic rollback on SLO breach.
3. If canary is green, a progressive rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100% over 72h) is initiated with telemetry-based automatic pause if p95 rises >10% from baseline.

Safety notes

- Never run overload probes on production serving clusters without explicit SRE approval. Use dedicated probe clusters that mirror topology instead.
- Always include a rollback plan and a pre-created hotpatch image if kernel regressions are suspected.

Troubleshooting common failure modes

- Missing traces: confirm that the probe-runner has write permissions to trace-ingest and that sampling rate is not 0.
- High variance between runs: check sequence-length distribution drift and re-run baseline with matched corpus.
- Kernel OOMs during overload: reduce batch sizes in the probe matrix and capture coredump + kernel telemetry.

Appendix: quick diagnostic commands

- Start a probe-run locally (dev cluster):
  ./tools/probe-runner --config probe-config.yaml --dry-run=false

- Extract probe artifacts:
  gsutil cp gs://benchmarks/probe-2026-02-08-crosslayer-01/*.ndjson ./local/

- See variance-driven-sampling-and-cost-correlation-playbook-2026 for sampling strategies and cost attribution.
